issues.description: The core RCE vector — arbitrary class instantiation via Class.forName(...).newInstance() on attacker-controlled type/flipstrategy names in PropertyFactory, XmlParser, YamlParser, PropertiesParser, MappingUtil, and ConsoleOperations — is entirely unaddressed. An attacker can still supply a malicious Property/FlippingStrategy type that gets instantiated, so the vulnerability class survives.

Patch modifies PropertyClass.java, a file the official fix does not touch, and adds no type-assignability (allowlist) check. It closes only the static-initializer-on-load gadget, not instantiation; it is not a superset or subset of the official fix but a differently-located, incomplete mitigation.

Execution evidence is weak: pov_before_reproduced=false and regressions_ran=0, so there is no demonstration that the patch actually blocks a working exploit or preserves behavior under the project's test suite.

result.summary: Our patch only rewrites PropertyClass.fromString to load classes without initialization (initialize=false), which defeats a single static-initializer gadget but leaves untouched every Class.forName(...).newInstance() sink the official fix hardens with type-assignability allowlists (PropertyFactory, XmlParser, YamlParser, PropertiesParser, MappingUtil, ConsoleOperations). The CWE-094 code-injection class therefore remains exploitable through arbitrary Property/FlippingStrategy instantiation. It is a symptom-level fix at a non-canonical location, not the root-cause allowlist defense-of-record, and the execution signals (POV never reproduced, 0 regressions run) provide no real evidence of protection.
result.root_cause: Untrusted, persisted/parsed class-name strings are passed to Class.forName and then instantiated via newInstance() without validating that the resolved type is an allowed Property/FlippingStrategy subclass, permitting arbitrary code execution.
